headline: Best Buy's holiday comps slip 0.8% on soft industry demand; memory-chip costs cloud a flat FY27 outlook.
guidance_note: FY27: revenue $41.2-42.1B, comps -1% to +1%, adj op margin 4.3-4.4%, adj EPS $6.30-6.60; Q1 comp ~+1%.
key_messages: Domestic comp -0.8% (vs +0.2%); revenue $13.81B missed, but adj EPS $2.61 beat.
Barry cited slightly softer industry demand in the holiday quarter; weak Nov-Dec, then stronger late Dec-early Jan.
Computing posted an 8th straight positive quarter (laptops, desktops); gaming grew but much slower than prior two quarters.
Memory-component demand is creating cost inflation and supply uncertainty, especially in computing - the main FY27 risk.
Domestic gross profit rate ~flat at 20.9% as Ads/Marketplace offset lower product margins.

consumer.big_ticket: Holiday demand for consumer electronics was slightly soft; shoppers concentrated on promotional periods.
consumer.pricing: Memory-chip cost inflation expected to lift computing prices and constrain supply in FY27.

macro_read: Holiday tech spending was lackluster and event-driven, and component inflation threatens to raise device prices; discretionary demand is flat at best.
